# Mary Stubbs

## Overview

- **Age:** Roughly eight to twelve years old throughout the events described  <sub>[v5 c5 P15](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0015), [v5 c5 P51](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0051)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c5 P1](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0001)</sub>
- **Status:** Orphan; foster child under the care of Miss Winifred (Mrs. Ambrose Kerr)  <sub>[v5 c5 P51](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0051), [v5 c9 P0](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0000), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)</sub>
- **Origin:** Hopetown Asylum  <sub>[v5 c5 P51](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0051)</sub>
- **Role:** Student; domestic helper for Mrs. Ambrose Kerr  <sub>[v5 c8 P0](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0000), [v5 c9 P4](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0004), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)</sub>

## Appearance

Mary is a slender girl with an unusually wide mouth, fine white teeth, and a pale, freckled, sun-browned face. She has light, pale blue eyes bordered by dark, thin rims, and limp, heavy flaxen hair that she wears in long braids. She is known to possess extremely sharp and perceptive ears, as well as a lively, mischievous grin.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P5](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0005), [v5 c5 P11](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0011), [v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c5 P26](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0026), [v5 c5 P58](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0058), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000)_

## Personality

Mary is an outspoken, sharp-tongued, and fiercely independent girl who refuses to tolerate condescension or pity. Having endured a harsh, abusive past, she masks her vulnerability with a bold, sarcastic, and boastful exterior, taking a defiant pride in her resilience and capacity for hard work. Beneath her rough, slang-laden mannerisms lies a deeply loyal and appreciative heart, capable of profound devotion toward those who treat her with genuine kindness. She is naturally observant and perceptive, frequently offering blunt, unfiltered critiques of community affairs.

_Sources: [v5 c5 P1](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0001), [v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c5 P28](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0028), [v5 c5 P58](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0058), [v5 c5 P126](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0126), [v5 c8 P0](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0000), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044), [v5 c11 P1](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0001), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000)_

## Goals

- To escape abuse and live in a safe, comfortable home  <sub>[v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c5 P108](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0108)</sub>
- To master skills and be recognized as capable and self-sufficient  <sub>[v5 c4 P59](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0059), [v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014)</sub>
- To protect and support her closest companions  <sub>[v5 c5 P53](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0053), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)</sub>

## History

Fleeing the severe cruelty of Mrs. Grimble, Mary ran away to Glen St. Agnes, where she hid in an old barn until discovered by the Ashdown children. Weak from starvation, she was brought to the manse, fed, and befriended by the minister's children, particularly forming a bond with Ida and Grace. Soon afterward, news arrived that Mrs. Grimble had died, leaving Mary free from her former bond. Fearing a return to the asylum or assignment to another harsh household, Mary found an advocate in Ida Ashdown, who pleaded her case to Miss Winifred (Mrs. Ambrose Kerr). Impressed by Mary's honesty and industrious nature, Mrs. Kerr took her in to live at her home, where Mary thrived under firm but compassionate care. Mary quickly adapted to her new life, taking pride in her domestic duties, joining the local school, and taking part in games in Fern Hollow alongside the Ashdown and Carrow children. Although she occasionally engaged in mischief—such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's collar in church or scaring children with ghost stories—she proved her loyalty by fiercely defending Mr.

## Background by volume

- Orphaned at a young age after her parents died  <sub>[v5 c5 P53](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0053)</sub>
- Spent two years in the Hopetown Orphan Asylum starting at age six  <sub>[v5 c5 P51](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0051), [v5 c5 P53](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0053)</sub>
- Taken in by Mrs. Grimble, an abusive woman over the harbour, where she suffered hard labor and frequent beatings for four years  <sub>[v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c5 P51](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0051), [v5 c8 P15](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0015)</sub>
- Escaped Mrs. Grimble's house and hid in the old Taylor barn near Glen St. Agnes  <sub>[v5 c5 P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 c5 P42](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0042)</sub>
